greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Peace be with you, and may the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, who gathers us in his love, be with you all.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you commanded us to love God with all our heart: Lord, have mercy.
Christ Jesus, you taught us to love our neighbor as ourselves: Christ, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you are the source of all our strength and our refuge: Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: I love you, Lord, my strength.
homily:
In the book of Exodus, we hear a command that seems, at first, like a simple instruction for daily living. 'You shall not wrong any widow or orphan,' the Lord says. 'If ever you wrong them and they cry out to me, I will surely hear their cry.' It is a stern warning, but it is also a profound revelation of the heart of God. He is the one who listens. He is the one who leans in close when the world turns away. He is the one who hears the cry of the vulnerable before the rest of the world has even noticed there is a need. We often think of God as a distant architect of the universe, but here, he is the intimate protector, the one who counts the tears and hears the prayers that are whispered in the silence of a kitchen or the quiet of a bedroom at 3 a.m.

Think of the image of the cloak. 'If you take your neighbor's cloak as a pledge, you shall return it to him before sunset; for this cloak of his is the only covering he has for his body.' It is a fragile, human image—a piece of fabric, a simple garment, the only thing standing between a person and the cold. It reminds us that God is deeply concerned with our basic, human needs. He cares about the comfort of our bodies, the security of our homes, and the warmth of our relationships. He does not want his children to be left out in the cold. He is the God who provides the covering.

Benjamin Vo knew something about the importance of being covered, of being held, and of being safe. He was a boy who understood that life is meant to be shared, and that we are meant to be a comfort to one another. You remember him, don't you? You remember that bright, inquisitive light in his eyes—the boy who could look at a complex piece of technology or a math problem and see not just a challenge, but a way to connect, a way to build, a way to make the world a little more understandable. He had that brilliant, analytical mind, but it was always, always tethered to a heart of immense kindness. He was a boy who looked at the world and saw people who needed to be cared for.

Alan and Thao, I know that for these four months, the silence of your home has felt like a long, cold night. You look at the space where Benjamin used to be, and you feel the ache of a covering that has been lifted. You wonder how to hold onto the warmth when the world feels so vast and so empty. I want to tell you something that is true: you are not out in the cold. You are still wrapped in the love that God has for you, and you are still wrapped in the love that Benjamin had for you. That love did not evaporate when he went home to God. It changed form. It became a part of the air you breathe, a part of the memories you share, a part of the very fabric of your family. You are still a family of four. That is a reality that is etched into the heart of God, and no distance, no time, and no silence can ever erase it.

In the Gospel today, the Pharisees try to test Jesus. They want to pin him down, to make him choose one law over another, to turn the faith into a checklist. But Jesus does something that completely undoes their game. He goes to the root. 'You shall love the Lord, your God, with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind. The second is like it: You shall love your neighbor as yourself.' He does not offer a new set of rules; he offers a new way of being. He tells us that the entire law, the entire purpose of our existence, is hung on the hook of love. Everything we do, every step we take, every breath we draw, is meant to be an act of love for God and for the people he has placed in our lives.

Benjamin lived this. He didn't need a rulebook to tell him to be kind. He didn't need a commandment to remind him to be a good son or a loyal brother. It was his nature. Think of the way he listened to his father's stories. Those stories were not just entertainment; they were a way for him to say, 'I am with you. I am listening. I value what you value.' He was a boy who understood that love is an act of attention. He gave his attention to his family, to his friends, and to the world around him. He was a boy who, in his own quiet way, was always reaching out, always trying to bridge the gap, always trying to make sure that no one felt alone.

Ryan, you are a brother who knows this better than anyone. You know the way the house feels, the way the memories are woven into the very fabric of your life together. You are the one who carries the legacy of his kindness. When you look at the sky, when you think of the planes, when you feel the quiet of the house, know that you are a vital part of this living mystery. You are the one who knows what it means to be a brother, to be a friend, to be a witness to the fact that love is the most durable thing we possess. Keep being the boy who reaches out. Keep being the one who sees the beauty in the small things. You are a witness to the world that love is stronger than any distance, that it is the most beautiful material in the universe.

There is a temptation, when we are hurting, to think that we have to be 'strong' in the way the world defines strength—that we have to be stoic, or silent, or that we have to 'get over' our grief. But Jesus does not ask for that kind of strength. He asks for the strength of the heart. He asks us to be like the widow and the orphan who cry out to him. He wants to hear your cry. He wants to hear your longing. He wants you to bring the empty chair to him and say, 'Lord, this is hard.' He is not offended by your tears. He is not put off by your questions. He is the one who is sitting with you in the quiet, and he is the one who is holding the cloak of his mercy around your shoulders.

Do you remember how Benjamin used to giggle when he talked about 'con chim airlines'? It was such a beautiful, simple, joyful thing. It was a dream of flight, of rising above the earth, of seeing the world from a different perspective. That is exactly where he is now. He is at the banquet of heaven, and he is looking down at you with that same sweet, gentle smile. He is not worried. He is not suffering. He is in the presence of the One who is the source of all love. And he is waiting for you. He is waiting for you to finish your journey, to keep your lamp lit, to keep your heart open, and to keep loving the way he loved.

We are living in a time that often feels like a long, cold autumn. We see the leaves falling, we feel the air turning, and we are tempted to look for security in the things we can control. But Jesus is inviting us to look at the Father. He is inviting us to trust that the ground we are standing on is holy. He is not distant. He is the one who is kneeling with you in the silence. He is the one who is holding your hand when the night is at its deepest. He is the one who is whispering to your hearts that you are not alone, that you are not forgotten, and that you are loved beyond all measure.

So, what do you carry out the door today? It is not a new set of plans. It is a simple, quiet, doable thing: keep your heart open to the love that is all around you. When you feel the ache, do not turn away from it. Let it be the place where God meets you. When you see someone who is struggling, when you see someone who is thirsty, when you see someone who is just trying to make it through the day, remember that they, too, bear the image of the Creator. Reach out to them. Give a little of your time, a little of your heart, a little of your kindness. Not because you have to, but because you are overflowing with the love that Benjamin left behind. You are the stewards of his legacy. You are the ones who keep the water moving, just as you have done with the 'Well of Love' in Vietnam. That well is a sign, a tangible, physical piece of the grace that you are living. It is a sign that the love that was poured into Ben is still flowing, still quenching the thirst of the poor, still bringing life to the dry places. Every time you are kind, every time you choose to hope, you are adding to that well. You are keeping the water moving. You are ensuring that the legacy of his gentle spirit continues to nourish the earth.

Do not be afraid of the future. The same God who held Benjamin in his hand as he looked out at the sky is the same God who holds you today as you look out at your own horizon. He is not a stranger. He is your Father. He knows the exact shape of your heart, he knows the depth of your longing, and he knows how much you miss the one you love. And he is promising you that the story is not over. The reunion is certain. Keep your eyes on the sky. Keep your heart in the light. And remember that he is waiting for you, and he is watching over you with that same sweet, gentle smile that you remember so vividly. That smile is a sign. It is a sign that the banquet is coming, and that the One who started this good work in you will surely bring it to completion. You are loved without limit, and you are being held by the same hands that hold him.

There is a story about a boy who once offered his entire piggy bank to help an uncle he loved. He didn't need to break it, he didn't need to empty it—the offer was the thing. It was the movement of a heart that was already generous, already sacrificial, already looking for ways to be a blessing. That is the heart of your son. That is the heart of your brother. That is the heart that God is shaping in you, too. When you offer your own grief, when you offer your own longing, when you offer your own service to the poor in his name, you are doing exactly what he would have done. You are keeping the love flowing.

So, do not worry about the 'why.' Do not worry about the 'how.' Just focus on the 'who.' Focus on the Lord who hears every cry. Focus on the brother who is waiting for you. Focus on the family that is still a family of four. And remember that the cloak of God’s love is the only covering you will ever need. It is warm, it is durable, and it is yours forever. Keep walking. Keep trusting. Keep loving. And know that you are held, you are seen, and you are loved beyond all measure. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you in his peace, and may the grace of our Savior lead you home. Go in the love of the Lord.
standing_petitions: For our beloved Benjamin, and for all who have gone before us, that they may rest forever in the radiant light of Christ's peace.
For all who carry the weight of grief, that the Lord may console them, strengthen their hearts, and fill them with the hope of the Resurrection.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
Thus says the LORD:
"You shall not molest or oppress an alien,
for you were once aliens yourselves in the land of Egypt. 
You shall not wrong any widow or orphan. 
If ever you wrong them and they cry out to me,
I will surely hear their cry. 
My wrath will flare up, and I will kill you with the sword;
then your own wives will be widows, and your children orphans.

"If you lend money to one of your poor neighbors among my people,
you shall not act like an extortioner toward him
by demanding interest from him. 
If you take your neighbor's cloak as a pledge,
you shall return it to him before sunset;
for this cloak of his is the only covering he has for his body. 
What else has he to sleep in?
If he cries out to me, I will hear him; for I am compassionate."

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (2) I love you, Lord, my strength.
I love you, O LORD, my strength,
O LORD, my rock, my fortress, my deliverer.
R. I love you, Lord, my strength.
My God, my rock of refuge,
my shield, the horn of my salvation, my stronghold!
Praised be the LORD, I exclaim,
and I am safe from my enemies.
R. I love you, Lord, my strength.
The LORD lives and blessed be my rock!
Extolled be God my savior.
You who gave great victories to your king
and showed kindness to your anointed.
R. I love you, Lord, my strength.

readings.label: Reading 2
readings.text:
Brothers and sisters:
You know what sort of people we were among you for your sake. 
And you became imitators of us and of the Lord,
receiving the word in great affliction, with joy from the Holy Spirit,
so that you became a model for all the believers
in Macedonia and in Achaia.
For from you the word of the Lord has sounded forth
not only in Macedonia and in Achaia,
but in every place your faith in God has gone forth,
so that we have no need to say anything. 
For they themselves openly declare about us
what sort of reception we had among you,
and how you turned to God from idols
to serve the living and true God
and to await his Son from heaven,
whom he raised from the dead,
Jesus, who delivers us from the coming wrath.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
When the Pharisees heard that Jesus had silenced the Sadducees,
they gathered together, and one of them,
a scholar of the law tested him by asking,
"Teacher, which commandment in the law is the greatest?" 
He said to him,
"You shall love the Lord, your God,
with all your heart,
with all your soul,
and with all your mind.
This is the greatest and the first commandment.
The second is like it:
You shall love your neighbor as yourself. 
The whole law and the prophets depend on these two commandments."

pet_prayers.text: Thinking of you buddy! Stop by to say hello whenever you can okay? Love you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - Been dreaming about you a lot. Hope you're having fun up in heaven. Please look after our family. Remember to come say hi daily. We miss you so much!

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever

pet_prayers.text: What happened my son? It's been 3 months since you left us. Missing you so much my whole body aches. Mom cries every day now... What are we going to do now Ben?  Please pray for us.
